messages:
maya-support: Customer reports repeated 500s on POST /v1/generate since 13:12 UTC. Got a stack of request IDs but need minimal repro and a quick smoke script. Example request id: rq_8f3a2b1e. Latency spikes to ~2.1s then 500. Any quick steps we should ask them to run?

tom-sre: Can you grab one full request-id with X-Request-ID from their header and the time window? We need: request id, region, model, and the exact payload. Also check if they proxied through our gateway. :eyes:

maya-support: Pasting what I have: model=redwood-large-v1, region=us-east-1, request id list: [rq_8f3a2b1e, rq_b2c4d5e6]. Payload is a simple completion with prompt ~120 tokens. Customer says error body: `\{"error\":\{"message\":\"internal server error\",\"type\":\"server_error\"\}\}`

ingrid: Ask them to run a tiny curl reproduction with a single token limit and include X-Request-ID so our logs line up. Example we can give them:```bash
curl -s -D - \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: smoke-$(date +%s)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-large-v1","input":"test","max_tokens":1}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```

ingrid: Also ask them to run the quick python/js/go variants so we can rule out SDK bug. Short snippets below.

maya-support: please include their stdout/stderr and the full response headers when they run it. Also request they run from their prod host if possible (to reproduce routing).

devlin: Adding the minimal snippets — keep them tiny so customer will run them immediately.

devlin: ```python
# python minimal
import os, requests
h={"Authorization":f"Bearer {os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY')}","X-Request-ID":"py-smoke-1234","Content-Type":"application/json"}
resp=requests.post('https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate',json={"model":"redwood-large-v1","input":"smoke","max_tokens":1},headers=h)
print(resp.status_code)
print(resp.headers)
print(resp.text)
```

devlin: ```javascript
// node minimal
const fetch = require('node-fetch')
;(async ()=>{
  const res = await fetch('https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate',{method:'POST',headers:{'Authorization':`Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}`,'X-Request-ID':'js-smoke-1234','Content-Type':'application/json'},body:JSON.stringify({model:'redwood-large-v1',input:'smoke',max_tokens:1})})
  console.log(res.status)
  console.log(await res.text())
})()
```

devlin: ```go
// go minimal
package main
import (
  "bytes"
  "fmt"
  "io/ioutil"
  "net/http"
  "os"
)
func main(){
  client:=&http.Client{}
  body:=[]byte(`{"model":"redwood-large-v1","input":"smoke","max_tokens":1}`)
  req, _ := http.NewRequest("POST","https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate",bytes.NewReader(body))
  req.Header.Set("Authorization","Bearer "+os.Getenv("REDWOOD_API_KEY"))
  req.Header.Set("X-Request-ID","go-smoke-1234")
  req.Header.Set("Content-Type","application/json")
  resp, err := client.Do(req)
  if err!=nil {fmt.Println("err:",err); return}
  b,_:=ioutil.ReadAll(resp.Body)
  fmt.Println(resp.StatusCode)
  fmt.Println(string(b))
}
```

maya-support: Great — also request a debug bundle from them if the smoke reproduces. Give them this command to upload logs (this calls our debug collection endpoint and returns an upload token):```bash
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/internal/debug/collect" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"request_id":"rq_8f3a2b1e","notes":"support escalation - 500s"}'
```

maya-support: If they can't hit that endpoint, ask for gzip'd logs from the time window and the app's outbound proxy logs.

tom-sre: If they paste the exact X-Request-ID (or the smoke run X-Request-ID), I'll correlate in logs and pull the kube pod and stack traces. If we see OOM or a kernel-level error we'll escalate to eng-runtime.

sdk-bot: Quick note: if they're on an older SDK (<1.4.0) ask them to run the curl variant — older SDKs had a keepalive bug that could show as intermittent 500s. See changelog: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/releases/tag/v1.4.0 :+1:

ingrid: Also request the cURL output with -i -v so we can see TLS handshake and any proxy 502s: `curl -v -i ...`

maya-support: I'll message the customer with the snippets and ask for one quick smoke run with the curl and the python snippet, and to upload a debug bundle if it reproduces. Back here with results. :thumbsup:
